TomTom Sees Breakthrough in Autonomous Driving Accelerating

2026-09-03 De Telegraaf TomTom, autonomous driving, self-driving cars, ADAS, map data, navigation, automotive, 2030 predictions
Read the source article

Quick summary

TomTom expects partially self-driving cars to break through rapidly, predicting that by 2030 approximately 60% of new cars sold in Europe will feature systems capable of largely autonomous steering, acceleration, and braking on highways.

Key takeaways

  • TomTom predicts ~60% of new European cars sold by 2030 will have systems enabling largely autonomous driving on highways
  • CEO Mike Schoofs sees 2026 as a transition year before revenue growth resumes, driven by automotive sector demand
  • The company positions its map data and real-time traffic information as essential infrastructure for autonomous driving systems
  • The prediction aligns with TomTom's CES 2026 focus on "mapping the road to autonomy" and powering the next era of driving
  • TomTom's automotive navigation now combines predictive logic, a proactive AI agent, and integrated EV routing
